title: Restoration Errors: Does Sycophantic Capitulation Persist After Pressure Is Removed?

original_idea.body: Restoration Errors. Problem: whether a model that capitulated to false pushback can be restored to truth when pressure stops is under-measured. Direction: multi-turn protocol (correct -> false pushback -> capitulation -> neutral re-query/'are you sure?'), measure recovery rate and neutral turns needed, characterize sticky vs recoverable capitulation across open models.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Strong chain: whether capitulation sticks determines downstream conversation contamination, a concrete harm dimension.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Tightly scoped recovery-rate metric with clear protocol.

low_compute.reasoning: Scripted dialogue on open models, cheap.

novelty.reasoning: The post-pressure recovery dimension appears mostly novel beyond progressive/regressive framing.

novelty_assessment.reasoning: Recovery-after-pressure (sticky vs recoverable capitulation) appears under-explored.
